scope: M2 JSHandle and ElementHandle base lifecycle, supported graph serialization, original-context evaluation and same-process frame evaluation. Functional verification only; no performance or release claim.

contract.values: Existing bounded graph values and exact UTF-16 property names/strings. Nested and repeated handles unbox with object identity; ElementHandles retain their exact DOM object after detachment. Browser Node/Document/Window values serialize to pinned reference descriptions, including inside graphs. Maps/functions/symbols can remain handles and be evaluated, but their by-value serialization remains explicitly unsupported.
contract.ownership: Object references remain in their original page/frame/unique context. Primitive values survive navigation and may cross live pages in the same engine. Destroyed object contexts free native slots; explicit disposal is idempotent. Property handles own separate native references and remain alive after parent or sibling disposal. New allocations are grouped privately, published only after reply encoding, and discarded on cancellation, output rejection or late caller success.
contract.bounds: At most 4096 retained or pending handles per page. Exhaustion rejects before user evaluation. Incomplete property allocation rolls back its private group. Ordinary CDP property replies retain their 8 MiB cap; application results obey negotiated bytes/depth/nodes. Cleanup has a separate 500 ms recovery budget and retires the affected page when its pending allocation cannot be recovered safely.
contract.intentionalDifference: SPECS S4.l: preserve primitive BigInt values. Pinned Playwright 1.60.0 converts its Chromium BigInt handle to undefined. Creation preview, jsonValue, argument passing and receiver evaluation are recorded separately, never counted as equal-result conformance or a speedup.

coverage: Nine shared browser groups cover ten primitive edge values, graph identity/cycles, nested handle arguments, Unicode properties, getter behavior, independent reference disposal, DOM detachment/reference values, nonserializable object evaluation, failures without replay, concurrent evaluation, foreign-object rejection, same-process frame ownership, navigation and page closure.

Seven native lifecycle/publication cases cover the 4096-slot bound, slot reuse after disposal/navigation, partial property rollback, cancelled shared preparation, timed-out synchronous and deferred allocations, rejected primitive output and ten repeated rejected property groups.
Caller-deadline fake-peer cases cover late success from all five allocation APIs and verify precise group discard before timeout rejection.

Fresh packed npm ESM/CommonJS consumers run handle operations and typecheck inferred unboxed arguments, property handles, element subtypes, asElement and frame evaluation with negative type assertions.

Raw CDP replies preserve escaped lone surrogates, reject oversized property payloads without corrupting subsequent replies, and discard late cancelled responses. The UTF-16 decoder tests every single UTF-16 code unit plus mixed escaped/literal text.
